title: FFI _where functions: populate attr[20] for C parity
description:
C's `swe_sol_eclipse_where` and `swe_lun_occult_where` internally call `eclipse_how` at the computed central point and fill `attr[20]` with local circumstances (magnitude, azimuth, altitude, Saros, etc.), then overwrite `attr[3]` with `dcore[0]` (core shadow diameter). The Rust FFI wrappers currently zero `attr[20]` because the lib crate's `EclipseWhere` struct only carries geographic/shadow-cone data.

This was correctly handled per swisseph-rs/135's escape hatch ("zero and document — do not add lib-crate computation"), and the header documents "zeroed — local circumstances require swisseph_sol_eclipse_how". But it's a C-parity gap that would surprise consumers porting from the original Swiss Ephemeris.

### Options
1. **FFI-level fix**: have the FFI `_where` wrappers make an additional `sol_eclipse_how` / equivalent call internally to populate attr. Pros: no lib change. Cons: extra computation the caller might not need; the FFI layer doing work the lib doesn't.
2. **Lib-level fix**: extend `EclipseWhere` to optionally carry attr data, computed during `sol_eclipse_where` / `lun_occult_where`. Pros: clean, mirrors C's internal structure. Cons: wider change.

### Files
- `swisseph-ffi/src/eclipse.rs` — `swisseph_sol_eclipse_where` (line ~297), `swisseph_lun_occult_where` (line ~733)
- `src/eclipse.rs` — `EclipseWhere` struct, `sol_eclipse_where`, `lun_occult_where` implementations
- `swisseph-ffi/tests/eclipse.rs` — add slot-by-slot attr tests for both _where functions"

acceptance_criteria.text: swisseph_sol_eclipse_where and swisseph_lun_occult_where populate attr[20] with local circumstances matching C's swe_sol_eclipse_where / swe_lun_occult_where output
Parity tests verify all 20 attr slots against the lib's sol_eclipse_how / equivalent output at the same central point

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex adversarial review (verdict: needs-attention)

Finding 1 [medium, CONFIRMED]: attr zeroed when _where returns no eclipse (swisseph-ffi/src/eclipse.rs:306-322, 765-780). The FFI gates eclipse_how_at on `!w.flags.is_empty()`, zeroing attr for retval=0. C calls eclipse_how unconditionally — golden data at JD 2451545.0 has retval=0 but non-zero attr (attr[0]=-103.62, attr[3]=-1423.20). FFI tests avoid this by only testing epochs with central eclipses. Same pattern duplicated in lun_occult_where.

Recommendation: Remove the flags.is_empty() short-circuit. After a successful _where call, always call eclipse_how_at. Add a retval=0 FFI test case using JD 2451545.0 to prevent regression.
